newsitem.title: USA: Grant in plan with Elliott to leave bankruptcy.
newsitem.headline: Grant in plan with Elliott to leave bankruptcy.

text.p: Grant Geophysical, operating in Chapter 11 bankruptcy, said Friday it signed a letter of intent with Elliott Associates LP to fund and jointly sponsor a plan of reorganization for Grant.

The company said Elliott would provide $30 million in new equity and provide $2 million in expanded credit facilities, while making available an additional $2.5 million in loans before the reorganization plan in completed.
The company, which will file the plan with bankruptcy court in Delaware May 15, expects the plan to be approved during the second quarter.

If the plan is completed, secured creditors would be paid in full with cash and/or notes. Unsecured creditors would receive payment in some combination of cash, notes, stock and credits exchangeable for services. Elliott would end up owning 51 percent of the company's common shares.

The company said in preliminary results, it lost $74 million in 1996, on revenues of $103 million, relating largely to writedwons, reserves and extraordinary expenses. Those charges amounted to $52 million.
Grant is traded on the "pink sheets" under the symbol GRNT.
